# Coherent Corp

## F1Q27 Review: Long-Term Outlook Takes Center Stage as Next-Gen Ramps Gain
Visibility; Reit. OW

  
---  
  
By Joseph Cardoso
AC,
Manmohanpreet
Singh,
Marc
Vitenzon

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
COHR, COHR US  
Price (04 Nov 26):$195.09  
Price Target (Dec-27):$385.00  
  
Through the F1Q27 (Sep-end) print, Coherent addressed key investor concerns by
providing updates in the form of long-term guidance for revenue and margins,
including drivers and milestones across the portfolio. In fact, the long-term
guide overshadowed the F1Q27 results and the F2Q27 guidance, both of which
tracked ahead of consensus expectations heading into the print, highlighting
robust demand and consistent execution. Management's commentary showed
continued progress on next-generation programs, including PhotonLink starting
to contribute small revenues in Dec-26 quarter, initially in CPO scale-out,
followed by a ramp towards $100 mn+ in the Mar-27 and $250 mn+ per quarter
before the end of CY27, with scale-up CPO/NPO shipments slated for 2H CY27.
Within the PhotonLink platform, Coherent highlighted a new LTA for $20 bn of
revenue over a period of five years, starting in early CY28, which is in
addition to the LTA with Nvidia. The newly announced program is related to a
NPO deployment and is anchored around the 400 mW CW laser (similar to Nvidia),
while also spanning several other products offered under the PhotonLink
platform. Management also disclosed scale-across/DCI revenue of $200 mn+ in
F1Q27 (~4x y/y or +53% q/q), along with guidance for it to ramp towards $400
mn+ per quarter by end of CY27, supported by the multi-rail ramp starting in
the Mar-27 quarter, where the company addresses the opportunity with
components, modules/line cards and complete solutions to NEM and hyperscaler
customers alike. Management tied the extended visibility from the new LTAs
running through the end of the decade in the form of a reiterated target of a
first $3 bn revenue quarter in FY27, a new guidance of 60%+ pro forma revenue
growth in FY27 (more than double FY26's rate), and a first $4 bn revenue
quarter in FY28. The outlook is further supported by the internal InP capacity
ramp, with capacity doubling y/y in F1Q27, a quarter ahead of the original
plan, and tracking towards more than doubling again by end of CY27, along with
secured substrates, 6-inch production in Zurich slated for 1H CY27 and further
expansion planned beyond CY27. Separately, gross margin progress so far
includes no tailwind from captive InP laser use, as the internal/external mix
in TRx has barely changed over the past year; however, increased confidence
relative to mix shift towards more use of internal InP lasers in TRxs, as well
as layering in of margin-accretive next-generation products, is driving
management to raise its gross margin target of 45%+ before the end of CY28,
vs. the long-term target of 42%+ provided only ~18 months ago. Net-net, we are
embedding the latest guidance into our model, which on average increases our
out-year earnings by 10%+. We reiterate our Overweight rating and Dec-27 PT of
$385.

  * F1Q27 (Sep-end) Results: Earnings beat driven by modestly better revenues and margins relative to consensus expectations. Revenues tracked to $2,370 mn (vs. consensus of $2,315 mn, JPMe of $2,390 mn and guidance in the range of $2.2-$2.4 bn) or a pro-forma growth of +56% y/y (vs. +42% y/y in F4Q26), including Datacenter & Communications revenue of $1,952 mn (vs. consensus of $1,881 mn and JPMe of $1,935 mn), further supported by datacenter growth of +85% y/y and communications growth of +84% y/y, partly offset by Industrial at $419 mn (vs. consensus of $453 mn and JPMe of $455 mn). Gross margins tracked at 40.6% (vs. consensus of 40.6%, JPMe of 40.5% and guidance of 39.5%-41.5%), which along with disciplined opex drove operating margins to 23.2% (vs. consensus of 23.0% and JPMe of 22.9%), translating into EPS of $2.09 (vs. consensus of $2.02, JPMe of $2.08 and guidance of $1.85-$2.05).
  * F2Q27 (Dec-end) Guide: Earnings guide tracked above both consensus and JPMe driven by better revenues and margins. Coherent guided revenues to $2.55-$2.75 bn (midpoint of $2,650 mn vs. consensus of $2,554 mn and JPMe of $2,567 mn), implying revenue growth acceleration to +57% y/y vs 50% y/y in F1Q27. Gross margins are guided at 40.0%-42.0% (midpoint of 41.0% vs. consensus and JPMe of 40.8%), along with operating expenses of $430-$450 mn (midpoint of $440 mn vs. consensus of $443 mn and JPMe of $440 mn), driving an implied operating margin guide of 24.4% at the midpoint (vs. consensus of 23.5% and JPMe of 23.7%), and an EPS guidance of $2.28-$2.48 (midpoint of $2.38 vs. consensus of $2.24 and JPMe of $2.30).

LTAs extend visibility to CY28, but back-end loaded ramps carry
risk  
---  
| | Reiterate Rating: NEUTRAL  
---  
PO:240.00 USD   |   Price:195.09 USD  
| Equity   |   05 November 2026  
---  
---  
---  
---  
Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * SepQ beat and DecQ guide 4%/6% above cons on DCC strength. FY27 growth seen above 60%, with a first $3bn quarter in FY27
  * New $20bn Photon Link LTA and DCI at a $1bn run-rate extend visibility into CY28, but the biggest ramps are back-end loaded
  * GM in line at 40.6% and the 45% target is possible CY28. EPS up 17%/18% for CY27/28, but PO cut to $240 on sector de-rating

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
Strong visibility, broadening growth, but maintain Neutral

COHR reported SepQ sales/pf-EPS of $2.37bn/$2.09, +2%/+4% vs. cons. DCC beat
by 6%, offsetting softer Industrial. DecQ was guided to $2.65bn/$2.38, +4%/+6%
vs. Street. Mgmt. now sees FY27 growth above +60%, a first $3bn sales quarter
as early as MarQ, and $4bn in FY28. We highlight: (1) visibility is unusually
strong, with CY27 essentially booked, orders extending into CY28 and a new
~$30bn, 5-year Photon Link LTA for scale-up NPO starting in early CY28; (2)
new growth areas are scaling, with DCI scale-across at a ~$1bn run-rate (~4x
YoY) on track to double by end-CY27, and Photon Link rising to >$100mn in MarQ
and >$250mn/qtr by end-CY27; and (3) 6-inch InP capacity doubled a quarter
early, supporting a GM target raised to >45% by end-CY28 from >42%. Net-net,
we raise CY27/28E pf-EPS by 17%/18% to $12.77/$17.63 but lower our PO to $240
from $400 on ~14x CY28 PE (vs. 17x prior), in line with optics peers at 13-14x
after the sector de-rating. We reiterate Neutral given uncertainty on the pace
of data center and optics build-out, with DCC at 82% of sales, and
vulnerability to execution risks around large opportunities that ramp mostly
in CY28+ and could be pushed out; and (3) less margin leverage, as even
400-500bps expansion in 2-3 years to mid-40% GMs could be viewed as modest vs.
other optical peers like LITE.

Likes: Photon Link, GM levers, independent supplier

We like: (1) Photon Link's breadth, with content of up to ~15K per 100T chip
across 10+ CPO, 10+ NPO, and 5+ chip-to-chip engagements; (2) multiple GM
levers including pricing (among bigger contributors this quarter), mix shift
to new products, and the internal InP shift that is still largely ahead; (3)
COHR's position as an independent optics partner after the MRVL/LITE deal,
which could present an advantage in areas like ultra-high perf. lasers.

Risks: capex intensity, supply execution, competition

(1) Capex of $776mn 9~33% of sales) rises again in DecQ, keeping FCF
constrained, with intensity likely elevated in the years ahead; (2) growth is
limited by supply, so any delay in the 6-inch InP ramp or the shift to
internal lasers would cap upside and pus out the margin benefit; (3) rising
competition, as Chinese suppliers add low power (~70mW) CW laser capacity and
SiPho/MEMS alternatives could challenge COHR's liquid-crystal OCS by CY28-29.

# Datadog

## F3Q26 Review: Revenue Drivers Accelerate While Guidance Is Tempered by
Large Customer and Early Renewals; Reiterate OW

  
---  
  
By Samik Chatterjee, CFA
AC,
Jaiden R
Patel,
Mashu
Nishi

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
DDOG, DDOG US  
Price (04 Nov 26):$188.72  
**▼** Price Target (Dec-27):$290.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$305.00  
  
Datadog demonstrated robust execution in F3Q26, underscored by revenue results
driven by broad-based strength, including an acceleration in revenue growth
for the customer cohort excluding AI-natives as well as for the business
excluding the single largest customer - which highlights that the broader
demand backdrop for Datadog products remains quite robust. While the share
price reaction is led by the company’s conservatism to assume only minimum
commits from the large customer despite their significantly higher spending
pattern in 3Q, the longer-term positives from the print, include: 1)
acceleration in the non-AI customer cohort to a high-30% growth rate, in our
estimate, implies a deepening of the relationship with customers through
adoption of a higher number of products on average; 2) early renewals with
higher commitments from customers in the quarter point to long-term plans for
higher consumption from customers; 3) Revenues with AI-natives, a customer
cohort with which Datadog has significant traction, grew 80%+ in our estimate
and now comprises high-teens of revenue; 4) broadening of the portfolio,
including now with fast-growing BitsAI, creates further opportunities for
upsell with existing customers over time; and 5) robust growth in
infrastructure monitoring around mid-30% y/y despite significant scale ($2B of
ARR) and further opportunities with more adoption across training workloads.
We believe Datadog's total addressable market is set to widen meaningfully as
AI training workloads broaden beyond hyperscalers and AI labs into AI/software
companies and, eventually, the broader enterprise base, an expansion the
company is proactively positioning for through continued product development
across Observability, Security, GPU-specific capabilities. We continue to
expect Datadog to report above-peer growth, justifying its premium valuation
multiple. We are tweaking our revenue/earnings estimates; we are lowering our
Dec-27 PT to reflect a lower valuation multiple while investors await
visibility relative to cycling some of the temporal headwinds, but see a
favorable opportunity with our Dec-27 price target of $290 still implying ~55%
upside from current levels.

  * 3Q26 (Sep-end) Results: Broad-based revenue growth and strong opex leverage drove the beat as platform adoption deepens. Revenue tracked to $1.197B or +35% y/y, ahead of JPMe at $1.144B and consensus of $1.143B and the guidance range of $1.135B-$1.145B, meeting the high-end of buy-side expectations based on our conversations. The results were broad-based, as revenue growth excluding AI-native customers accelerated for the fifth consecutive quarter to the high-20% range and growth excluding the company’s largest customer also accelerated. RPO increased +38% y/y to $3.85B and cRPO also grew +38% y/y, driven by a mix of higher duration and early renewals. NRR remained in the low-120% range, and gross retention remained in the mid- to high-90% range. Platform adoption also continues to deepen, with 61% of customers using four or more products (vs. 54% a year ago), 41% using six or more (vs. 31%) and 16% using ten or more (vs. 8%), and infrastructure monitoring surpassing $2B of ARR with growth in the mid-30% range. Profitability was a bright spot in the print, with PF operating margin of 28% landing ~470bps above the guidance midpoint and PF EPS of $0.81 ahead of the $0.63-0.65 guidance range for 3Q and consensus estimate of $0.66.
  * 4Q26 (Dec-end) Guidance: Revenue outlook is modestly below expectations, continues to de-risk around the largest customer, while underlying growth excluding that customer remains healthy. Datadog issued 4Q revenue guidance of $1.19B-$1.20B, with the midpoint landing slightly below JPMe and consensus of $1.2B, and well below buy-side expectations. The guidance implies revenue growth of +25% y/y compared with JPMe and consensus at 26%. The moderation from 35% growth in 3Q is notable, although guidance contemplates only the contractual minimum from the company’s largest customer, despite usage remaining above that level in 3Q. Excluding this customer, the outlook implies growth in the low- to mid-30% range, which would also represent a degree of conservatism relative to their 3Q performance even though there are modest sequential headwinds from contract extensions / renewals with several large customers which incorporate commitment-based discounts. While 4Q includes large marketing investments, including AWS re:Invent, the PF operating income guidance of $280-$290M or 24% at the midpoint landed above JPMe and consensus at 23%. PF EPS guidance of $0.69-$0.71 is also ahead of JPMe of $0.65 and consensus of $0.67. 
  * FY26 (Dec-end) Guidance: Outlook revises higher to flow-through more than the 3Q beat, although tempered by early renewal activity. Revenue increased by $60M at the midpoint (relative to the $57M 3Q beat) to $4.52B (vs. JPMe of $4.47B, consensus of $4.48B, and prior midpoint guidance of $4.46B). The guidance now implies revenue growth of 32% compared to JPMe of 30%, consensus of 31%, and the prior outlook of 30%. Management notes that while its guidance philosophy hasn’t changed, the early renewal dynamics is a new phenomenon since last quarter, which while positive long-term, does create a headwind in the short term for revenue, limiting further upside. The PF operating margin guidance was revised higher by approximately 100bps to 24% relative to JPMe and consensus of 23%. PF EPS guidance increased to $2.73-$2.75 from $2.52 prior, compared with JPMe of $2.54 and consensus of $2.53. 
  * Key modeling notes from the callback (please reach out for more detailed notes). AI-native customers are growing faster than the overall business, implying AI-native NRR is above the companywide low-120% level. Early renewal discounts remain tied to commitment volume and contract duration and could move revenue growth by ~1-2 points, with no meaningful gross margin impact expected. The 4Q guidance reflects a short-term headwind related to early customer renewals combined with normal seasonality, as consumption softens from ~December 15 into January.

At sub-40x CY27 FCF for growth that remains 30%+ and no clear MT growth
challenge, we remain Buy-rated.  
|  |  | Global Research   
04 November 2026  
---|---|---  
| Datadog Inc| ●| (DDOG.O) Buy|  
---|---|---|---  
| Thoughts on the 4Q
Guide  
---  
| At sub-40x CY27 FCF for growth that remains 30%+ and no clear MT growth
challenge, we remain Buy-rated.  
  
| | Read Report   > |   
---|---  
| Summary Datadog posted a roughly in-line 3Q26 print, with revs growth of 35%
(slightly higher-than-normal 4.5% beat, roughly stable with 36% growth in
2Q26) landing right on top of our estimate while OMs (of 28%) and EPS were
above. The -14% move in the stock is in our view a reaction to the
disappointing 4Q26 revs guide, even if the explanation (customers renewing
early to capture discounted pricing) seems benign. We remain Buy-rated and
note that Datadog’s CFO is presenting at the upcoming UBS Tech & AI Conference
in Scottsdale in early-Dec. What Datadog Said As context, Datadog guides
relatively conservatively and typically walks-up its 4Q revs guide on the 3Q
call. This time it did not, instead reaffirming (not raising) the guide for
4Q26 revs of $1.20 billion. Even with a 4% beat on that guide, 4Q26 revs
growth would land at 31%, still solid but a sharper-than-expected decel from
35% in 3Q26. That’s the crux of today’s concern. Datadog said that overall
demand and usage trends remain strong but that a larger-than-expected number
of customers (AI-natives as well as other tech firms) did early-renewals in
order to capture more unit price discounts, weighing on revs growth near-term
but representing a positive long-term/2027 as these customers are signing
larger or longer-term deals in order to get these discounts. Datadog said that
these customers are spending well above their Datadog commits and did not pull
forward renewals due to budget pressures. What Else Could be Going On? In our
view there is no evidence of churn or (outside of OpenAI) any rising
competitive pressure. The only other plausible root cause of more customers
seeking price discounts is that they are indeed under more budget pressure.
Customer AI spend in 1H exceeded plans and this could have resulted in 2H
pressures, rival Dynatrace saw deal delays and hyperscaler growth (notably AWS
and Google Cloud) slowed. Moreover, Datadog said that their largest customer
(OpenAI) landed quite a bit higher than their minimum spend in 3Q26 and this
could have boosted the 3Q26 beat (in our view, raising the potential that the
core enterprise beat could have been normal/lower). Net, to be careful, we’re
trimming our 2027 revs growth estimate from 27% to 25%. Valuation: At 12x/39x
our 2027e rev/FCF estimates, we like the MT growth potential but concerns
about the initial 2027 guide could weigh on the stock through the 4Q26 print
in early-Feb. We’re trimming our PT from $320 to $275, which is based on 43x
CY28E EV/FCF (51x prior), a deserved premium to the comp group.

# Arm Holdings Plc

## Licensing Carries the Quarter as Royalties Remain Soft on Mobile; Higher
Confidence on $2B AGI CPU Chip Sales In CY27

  
---  
  
By Harlan Sur
AC,
Akanksh
Chauhan,
Apoorva
Kumar

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
ARM, ARM US  
Price (04 Nov 26):$191.80  
**▼** Price Target (Dec-27):$245.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$255.00  
  
ARM delivered a solid F2Q27 beat, with licensing strength offsetting softer
smartphone-related royalties, while the AGI CPU narrative continued to improve
as the company’s focus shifts from securing supply to execution. F2Q revenue
of $1.44B (+27% Y/Y) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 came in ahead of the
$1.38B/$0.47 guidance midpoints, with OPM expanding ~300bps Y/Y to 44.2%.
Licensing revenue (+50% Y/Y to $773M) was the standout, landing above guidance
on several large agreements (3 new ATAs + 4 new CSS licenses spanning DC and
smartphones) and continued backlog conversion. A new SoftBank project
(predominantly a DC XPU accelerator program) also lifted the licensing/design-
services run-rate to $209M per quarter. Royalty revenue (+8% Y/Y to $670M)
came in below expectations, with the shortfall being largely mobile-driven:
data center royalties doubled Y/Y for a third consecutive quarter and physical
AI grew +50% Y/Y, while Edge AI was roughly flat as higher memory pricing
weighed on mid/low-tier smartphone units (partly offset by Armv9/CSS royalty
rate uplift). Looking ahead, the F3Q guide of $1.54B/$0.56 at the midpoints
implies licensing growth of just over +50% Y/Y, offsetting more modest low-
single digit royalty growth against a difficult mobile compare. Management
indicated it expects similar total Y/Y revenue growth in F4Q27, albeit with a
more balanced license/royalty mix as ARM laps the memory-driven headwinds, and
sees mobile royalties returning to double-digit growth next year on roughly
flat units, supported by increasing CSS penetration and higher royalty rates.
More importantly, the AGI CPU opportunity continues to firm up, with purchase
orders from multiple customers and additional supply increasing management’s
confidence in its revenue targets, while first commercial deliveries remain on
track for F4Q27, which in total drove management’s increased confidence in
achieving up to $2B of revenue across FY27/FY28 (from >$1B last quarter).
Moreover, on our callback, management commentary indicated that demand remains
well above this level (Meta and the two AI model companies alone want more
than is embedded in the forecast), with focus now increasingly falling on
production execution and customer deployment, although the quarterly delivery
ramp and software readiness remain focal points ahead of the F3Q print. While
management appears comfortable with street estimates remaining well below $2B
until shipments begin, it alluded that any upside to both the FY27/FY28
framework and the prior $2B FY29/$5B FY30 trajectory is likely to be addressed
with F3Q earnings and at the next Arm Everywhere event (May/June). Beyond
these short-term dynamics, ARM expects DC royalties to sustain triple-digit
growth over the next few years on continued Graviton/Vera/Cobalt ramps, rising
core counts, and the transition of accelerator head-node CPUs from x86 to Arm,
potentially placing data centers on a path to pass mobile royalties in the
long-term. We are raising our forward estimates to reflect the license and
continued AGI CPU momentum, and are lowering our Dec-27 PT to $245 (from $255
prior) on lower peer multiples. We reiterate our Overweight rating.

  * F2Q delivered a clean beat on license strength, DC royalty doubling Y/Y again... Sep-Q revenue of $1.44B (+27% Y/Y) came in above the guidance midpoint of $1.38B, as did EPS of $0.52 (vs. street $0.47). Royalty revenue was up +8% Y/Y to $670M, a deceleration from F1Q +22% Y/Y and below the low-teens% Y/Y growth implied in the guide. Cloud AI was again the largest contributor to royalty growth, with DC royalty doubling Y/Y for the third consecutive quarter on continued Arm-based server CPU deployment at hyperscalers (Google Axion, AWS Graviton, Microsoft Cobalt, NVIDIA Vera). As a result, Arm’s server share at the top hyperscalers is now expected to exceed 60% by the end of CY26 (from >50% in CY25). Edge AI royalty was roughly flat Y/Y, as higher memory pricing continued to weigh on smartphone units, offset by higher royalty rates from continued Armv9/CSS adoption. Physical AI royalty grew +50% Y/Y on continued ADAS + in-vehicle adoption and expanding robotics deployment. License and other revenue grew +50% Y/Y to $773M, reflecting several large agreements signed in the quarter, 3 new Arm Total Access agreements, 4 new CSS licenses, and continued backlog contributions. 
  * F3Q guide implies continued ~24% Y/Y revenue growth, with license strength again more than offsetting mobile-driven royalty weakness… F3Q revenue was guided to $1.54B at the midpoint (vs. street $1.53B). Management expects F4Q27 Y/Y revenue growth to be similar to F3Q, albeit with a more balanced license/royalty contribution as ARM begins to lap the memory-driven mobile headwinds, allowing underlying tailwinds (Armv9, CSS rate uplift, datacenter ramps) to become more visible. Taken together, the outlook implies FY27 revenue of $6.1B by our math (vs. prior $6.0B). Within that, license tracks to ~+35-40% Y/Y (vs. prior +25-30%), offsetting weakness in royalty growth. Looking into next year, management sees mobile royalties returning to double-digit+ growth on roughly flat units. That outlook is supported by Armv9 penetration now >50%, rising CSS adoption, and higher royalty rates on next-gen CSS, while DC royalties are expected to grow triple digits over the next few years. 
  * Raising estimates; lowering Dec-27 PT to $245... We raise our FY27/FY28 estimates and lower our Dec-27 PT to $245 (from $255 prior). Given the company's new silicon CPU strategy and strong growth outlook, ARM is now growing significantly faster than peers (CDNS, SNPS). Peers are trading at a 1.6x-2.0x PEG ratio, and we assume earnings growth for ARM (using CY30 financial targets) drives a 40% EPS CAGR over the next 5 years. Applying a 1.8x PEG ratio (midpoint of the peer range) implies that ARM should trade at 1.8 x 40, or ~72x our FY28 EPS estimate of $3.40, or a $245 price target.

Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Reit. Neutral on Licensing outgrowth suggesting future Royalties, but N-T setup and AGI supplies more challenged. PO now $230
  * Likes: continued Licensing momentum, rising custom CPU demand/adoption, AGI CPU demand/POs from multiple customers

Strong Licensing offsets Royalties, AGI CPUs still limited

Modest beat/raise quarter mostly driven by stronger Licensing offsetting
weaker Royalties. Licensing is a leading indicator of future Royalties (12-24
months), suggests continued strong customer interest in custom silicon
solutions. However, Royalties remain pressured on weaker Edge AI (still
~60-70% of Royalty sales). Even with data center (DC) doubling YoY, we don't
see the needle moving much until the long-awaited AGI CPU chips start ramping
in FQ4 (MarQ'27). For AGI, mgmt is now more confident in reaching up to $2bn
of AGI CPU sales over FY27-28, but we continue to flag supply availability
remains the biggest challenge for ARM, as a new subscale entrant likely
disadvantaged versus incumbents AMD/INTC/NVDA, limiting the potential upside.
Overall, we modestly tweak FY26-28E by 0%-6% to $2.24/$3.04/$4.11, reiterate
Neutral. We lower PO to $230 (from $260) on lower sector/peer multiples: now
value CY30E IP at 1.7x PEG (vs. 2.0x) and chips at 15x PE (vs. 21x),
discounted back to CY28.

Likes: Licensing momentum, custom CPU/AGI demand

(1) Licensing momentum remains strong with ARM signing 3 new ATA customers
(now ~63 active) and 4 new CSS licensees (2 DC, 2 smartphone). DecQ Licensing
is guided up 50%+ YoY again. (2) The desire to build custom CPUs continues to
rise, with multiple customers ramping their own ARM CPUs throughout FY27 and
into FY28 (GOOGL Axion, AWS Graviton, MSFT Cobalt, NVDA Vera). Arm's server
share at top hyperscalers is set to exceed 60% exiting CY26 (from >50% in
CY25), with >100% YoY DC royalty growth for several years. (3) AGI CPU demand
remains high, with POs from multiple customers now running through CY27, and
OCI planning to offer AGI CPU instances in 2027.

Risks: Edge AI mix, phone units, AGI supply availability

(1) Despite the ramp of servers, Cloud AI is still only ~20% of royalties,
with the majority still Edge AI (~60-70% of Royalties). (2) Memory costs
continue to impact phone units, especially mid/low tier, with third party
estimates pointing to flattish YoY in CY27. Arm aims to outgrow the market by
~10%+ on v9/CSS adoption, though risks of extended unit weakness remain. (3)
Supply is the key constraint for AGI CPUs ramp. As a new, subscale entrant,
Arm is likely disadvantaged in securing wafers, substrates, memory and test
capacity versus incumbents AMD/INTC. First-gen GMs are only 30-40%, dilutive.

# Expedia Group, Inc.

## Solid 3Q Beat Across the Board, but 4Q Lower On Choppy Macro & Lapping
Impacts; Remain Neutral, & PT to $315

  
---  
  
By Doug Anmuth
AC,
Dae K Lee,
CFA,
Neeraj S Kookada,
CFA

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Neutral  
---  
EXPE, EXPE US  
Price (04 Nov 26):$315.88  
**▼** Price Target (Dec-27):$315.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$330.00  
  
EXPE reported solid 3Q results, exceeding the high end of both top and bottom
line expectations. Gross bookings grew 11% to $34.0B & revenue +12% to $4.9B,
both ahead of guidance. EXPE highlighted that consumer demand remained
healthy, especially in the US, w/room nights up 7%. B2B GBs grew +19%, while
consumer GBs were up +7% & accelerated in the US. We highlight that part of
the 3Q beat was due to EXPE pulling forward the Fall sales event in Sept vs.
Oct last year, and it generated $1B+ in GBs. Adj. EBITDA was $1.7B (+17% Y/Y),
w/ margins expanding +135bps Y/Y to 34.2%, ahead of expectations & the guide.
However, the 4Q outlook implies a notable decel — GBs +3.3%-5.2% & revenue
+4.0%-5.7% bracketed our prior 5% growth for GBs & revenue, respectively. Key
drivers of 4Q topline decel include: 1) Fall sale moving into 3Q; 2) Softer
backdrop from the US election cycle & geopolitical disruption in EMEA/the
Middle East, including long-haul routes; & 3) B2B lapping large partner
promotions from 4Q25. Mgmt expects room nights growth to be positive but
modest at ~0-2% & ADR to keep moderating, with investors concerned about
whether B2C room nights grow at all in 4Q. 4Q margins should also moderate on
slower revenue growth, less fixed-cost leverage, & investment from recent
acquisitions. We lower our 4Q GB by 1% to $28.2B (+5% Y/Y), keep our revenue
flat at $3.7B, (+5% Y/Y), and lower our Adj. EBITDA by 4% to $876M (23.5%
margin). Our key takeaways include: 1) AI-native/AEO channels are a promising
L-T growth lever—Traffic from the new Google AI Mode & Meta Muse integrations
remains small but high intent, & 3P data shows EXPE leading US AI citation
share. EXPE’s on-platform AI is already lifting engagement, conversion, &
booking size: natural-language search, compare/property-expert agents, & an
activity agent whose users are 2x as likely to book an activity within 7 days.
We view a more fragmented top of the funnel as a net positive for EXPE given
its edge in supply, pricing, payments, & servicing; 2)B2B remains a durable
share-gainer despite rising competition with DD% growth in every region, and
EXPE now has ~75K partners & the CarTrawler/Tiqets deals reinforce the one-
stop travel shop. That said, we expect some near-term B2B margin pressure as
partners move into higher volume tiers & one-stop-shop investments ramp;
3)Margin expansion is intact but non-linear. After a record 3Q, we expect 4Q
to moderate on slower growth, B2B investment, & slower consumer marketing
leverage (benefiting in ‘25 from cutting inefficient spend). Still, margins
expand >400bps from 2024 through the 2026 guide, and we see room for further
gains in '27; & 4)We view the 4Q decel as largely transitory. Fall Sales pull
forward, the election cycle, & tough B2B comps explain much of the decel. EXPE
noted it outperformed peers in 3Q (slightly ahead of BKNG) & expects to be
more in line in 4Q, so part of the decel also reflects how strong 3Q was for
EXPE. Coming out, we raise our ‘26E & ‘27E GBs, revenue, & Adj. EBITDA
estimates by 0-3%. We remain Neutral rated, and note that while 3Q was strong,
4Q outlook could raise some concerns. Our December 2027 PT goes to $315 (vs.
$330 prior), based on ~12x our ‘28E GAAP EPS of $26.57.

## Market Colour

Blue wave at the ballot box = red and green waves on our screens. Broad
strength with SPX +1.6% on volume 50% above average, yet NDX +91bps is a 3m
rel low and SOX -3.1% at a 6m rel low. The Dem vote has been taken as a public
vote against data centres, with notable candidates that have been advocating
moratoriums, including Gina Hinojosa in Texas, Amy Acton in Ohio and Keisha
Lance Bottoms in Georgia winning some key seats.AMZN +6% and MSFT +7% were the
clear winners yesterday. If Governor-elect Hinojosa delivers the promised
moratorium on new Texas data centre approvals, existing capacity gets scarcer,
and that seems to be the trade. AWS 2027 capacity is 'largely sold out' per
Jassy, with a $578bn backlog, and MSFT is also facing shortages. But if
compute is going to become incrementally harder to get online, you want to own
whoever already has it - plus any sense of capex moderating and FCF inflecting
helps the Hyperscalers. Especially in a scenario where they don't lose market
share.The worst? Highly concentrated Texas build-out exposure. HUT -23% and
CIFR -20%. CIFR alone has a 5.9GW development pipeline and a $9.1bn Barber
Lake lease. Neoclouds followed (CRWV -10%, IREN -11%, CORZ -10%). High-beta
optical and networking were weak too (MRVL -7%, LITE -8%, CIEN -9%, CRDO -10%,
CLS -9%) on the capex overhang. We get the sense a lot of the moves were
exacerbated due to de-grossing.Asia has picked up the semis selling. KOSPI -5%
with Samsung -8% and Hynix -9%, TWSE -3.2% with TSMC -89bps holding up better,
and Nikkei -1.8% with Advantest -15% and Tokyo Electron -9% (TOPIX +1.2%
though, so very much a chip selloff). Hang Seng Tech +5.3%, Tencent +7%,
Alibaba +8%, both benefit from a softer US regulatory stance.**And finally...
We're hosting two events today worth flagging**
